differences.what: massing: the draft's 12.5 x 6.5 m box with a one-storey bay is now the sheet's '3B' body across the whole 7.62 m lot under a flat roof, its party lines at x 248 and 615 px against the print's 250 and 612

the bay: three faces carried through the basement and all three storeys up to the main cornice, the cornice turned round it; its edges at x 410 and 553 px against 411 and 550, one arched light to each face a storey, a band at each storey, laid in channelled courses as the print's
the lights over the door: arched, 0.9 m wide, their heads at y 190 and 335 px against the print's 185 and 330, each under an arch band with a key block
the door: a pair of leaves under an arched fanlight in a segmental head, 1.64 m wide, as the print's double door with its transom
the door hood: a pediment on a stone entablature over two scrolled consoles, its apex at y 455 px against 452 and 2.7 m across
the cornice: the crown at y 50 px against the print's 48, about 1.8 m from the frieze's foot to the crown, carried round the bay

the arched basement light under the bay's front, half hidden by a shrub in the print, is not cut: K08 lays one light to each face of a storey and the bay's lowest storey runs from grade (L-k01-2033-otis-3659)

the flat front's channelled courses: the print lays the whole front in channelled courses about 0.3 m high; K01 lays a street wall smooth or rock-faced, so the build's flat front is smooth ashlar (the bay alone is channelled). A street visitor sees the banding, so it stays open until K01 can lay a channelled street wall (L-k01-2033-otis-3659)

the stoop's run: the print's yard stands above the public walk and its stoop runs down past the fence line to the walk (its foot at y 805 px); the build sets the yard on the town's grade and its stoop stops at the yard, its foot at about y 750. A visitor would see a stoop half the print's length, so it stays open until the yard's level above the walk is built (L-k01-2033-otis-3659)
the fence: K11's spear fence stands about 1.3 m with taller posts against the print's plain pickets about 0.9 m on their curb, about 0.4 m higher than the print's
the urn on the hood's apex is not built (K01 keeps a hood clear of the light over it, before whose foot the urn stands), and the hood stands about 0.15 m under the print's

carving finer than the print: the hood's consoles and frieze, the key blocks, the bay's spandrels and the cornice's frieze, built as plain members at the print's sizes; the consoles 1.0 m to the print's about 1.3
the cornice's brackets stand at the kit's spacing, wider apart than the print's close-set brackets, at the print's depth
tone: the build's buff Lemont limestone and its green sash against a monochrome print, which reads the stone pale and the sash dark

the neighbours: the print shows the row's two neighbours gone (a vacant lot and a 1940s loft to the north, a tower to the south); in 1904 2031 and 2035 stood against both party walls, so the build is right not to show the print's surroundings
the flanks, rear, roof and rear range, which the print does not see

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
